finding: On 1991-2026 history, more leverage always won: S&P 500 + SMA10 at 3x made 24.5%/yr (max DD -66%). But the forward simulation at today's valuations showed leverage does not raise the median.
decision: Leverage should follow the expected premium (Kelly: f = premium / variance). Try valuation-scaled leverage; widen leverage grids; lever the bond sleeve alone.
sources: Gayed & Bilello (2016) Leverage for the Long Run; Kelly (1956)

finding: Valuation-Kelly had the best TRAIN growth (13.8%/yr) but delevered through the 1991-2026 bull (test 14.9%). Expected wealth rises with leverage while median growth peaks near 2x (S&P+SMA10) or 2.5-3x (60/40+SMA10).
decision: Map the expected-value frontier so the leverage choice is explicit. Rank only strategies an ordinary margin account can hold (<=2x) separately from futures-only ones.
sources: Harvey et al. (2018) The Impact of Volatility Targeting; Ayres & Nalebuff, Lifecycle Investing

finding: Deployable champion: S&P 500 + SMA10 x2: 14.4%/yr since 1957, 18.1% on the untouched test period, max DD -47%, a 1987-style crash day costs -41%. Forward at CAPE 41: median 4.3%/yr (best of the frontier), mean wealth 1.83x in 10 years.
decision: Start forward paper accounts (deployable champion, research champion 60/40+SMA10 x3, 60/40 benchmark). Next: alternative trend signals under leverage, financing via leveraged ETFs (daily-reset decay), regime-specific leverage caps.

finding: Drawdown brake (test 21.2% vs 24.5% for plain 3x) and levered dual momentum (train picked 1x) lost. Seasonal leverage (3x Nov-Apr, 1x May-Oct) had the best TRAIN growth of any levered strategy (12.4%) and a smaller crash-day loss, but Sell-in-May largely vanished after its 2002 publication (t = 0.42 for 2003-2026). Valuation-scaled leverage to 3x: 15.7% test, max DD -42%.
decision: Champion unchanged. Seasonality goes on a watch list, not into the portfolio. Next: model leveraged-ETF daily-reset costs exactly with daily data, lifecycle de-leveraging, and combining the valuation and trend signals in one leverage rule.
sources: Bouman & Jacobsen (2002) The Halloween Indicator; Antonacci (2014) Dual Momentum Investing

finding: Recovery leverage (S&P 500 at 2x above its 10-month average, 3x while still >15% below its 36-month high) beat the 2x champion in training (11.6% vs 10.6%) and test (19.0% vs 18.1%), in all 12 depth/boost settings, with a higher forward median, higher average wealth and a lower chance of a 10-year loss. Variance management (Moreira-Muir) raised test growth only with more leverage and a lower forward median. Exp 16: a 2x/3x daily-reset S&P ETF matches cheap margin (+1.5%) and clearly beats retail margin (+5%), so up to 3x is reachable without a margin loan.
decision: New champion: recovery leverage (2x/3x via SSO/UPRO-style ETFs, cash otherwise). Added a 'deployable via ETFs' flag. Opened a forward paper account for it; the old 2x account continues as the margin champion. Next: when to exit faster in crashes (daily signal with a band), and a stock/bond version of recovery leverage.
sources: Moreira & Muir (2017) Volatility-Managed Portfolios; Poterba & Summers (1988); Exp 6, Exp 16
